relationships.subject: MCC950
relationships.evidence_quote: It specifically inhibited NLRP3 activation but not other inflammasome activation, including NLRP1, NLRC4, or AIM.

relationships.subject: MCC950
relationships.evidence_quote: Pharmacological blockade of NLRP3 by intrathecal delivery of the specific NLRP3 antagonist MCC950 reduced IL-1β overproduction and glial activation in ipsilateral SCDH as well as mechanical allodynia of CPIP model rats

relationships.subject: Caspase-1
relationships.evidence_quote: The active caspase-1 ultimately cleaves pro-IL-1β and pro-IL-18, leading to maturation and release of IL-1β and IL-18 with proinflammatory activities [25].

relationships.subject: TLR
relationships.evidence_quote: This process results in upregulation of inactive NLRP3 and pro-IL-1β transcription via nuclear factor kappa B (NF-κB)-mediated transcriptional regulation [25].

relationships.subject: HMGB1
relationships.evidence_quote: Nerve injuries can result in neuron damage, apoptosis, or death that release an array of DAMPs (e.g., HMGB1, IL-33, and ATP) to initiate NLRP3 inflammasome activation [37, 38].

key_findings: NLRP3 inflammasome is activated in local tissues, DRG, spinal cord and brain in chronic pain models and contributes to IL-1β overproduction and glial activation.
Blocking NLRP3 with MCC950 alleviates pain in CIPN, CRPS-I, EAE and other chronic pain models.
